meta_title: Installer Options: Install VpnHood! SERVER in a Script | VpnHood!
meta_description: The options of the VpnHood! SERVER install commands, on Linux and with Docker: install in a script without questions, or keep the server from starting at boot or updating itself.
title: Installer options
lead: The install commands ask a few questions as they run. Their options answer them in advance, so a script can install the server with no one at the keyboard.
linux_questions: The standalone install command asks three questions: [autostart_prompt_linux], [autoupdate_prompt_linux] and [min_protocol_prompt_linux]. For the first two, Enter picks the capital letter: yes on a new install, and on a server installed before, what it does now. For the third, Enter keeps the server's minimum, [min_protocol_default] on a new install, which lets every app in.
opt_q: No questions. Without the options below, a new install starts at boot, updates itself and lets every app in, and a server installed before keeps its choices.
opt_no_autostart: Answers no to the first question: the server does not start at boot. A new install then has no service, so you start the server yourself.
opt_no_autoupdate: Answers no to the second question: the server does not update itself.
opt_min_protocol: Answers the third question with a number from [min_protocol_default] to [min_protocol_proof]: the oldest app protocol the server accepts. Turn away probes says when to set [min_protocol_proof]. A managed server takes its minimum from its server profile.
opt_help: Lists the options, and installs nothing.
linux_add: Options go at the end of the install command, inside its quotes.
caption_linux: For example, in a script, with no questions
linux_change: To change an answer later, run the install command again, without [flag_quiet], and give the new answer. The server keeps its settings and access keys, and is updated to the latest release.
docker_question: The Docker install command asks one question: [docker_prompt]. Type [answer_yes] to have it install Docker and its compose plugin, which it can do on Ubuntu, Debian and the distributions based on them, or [answer_no] if the machine has them already.
opt_install_docker: Answers yes to the question: installs Docker and its compose plugin, unless the machine has them already.
opt_docker_q: No question: Docker is installed only with [flag_install_docker].
caption_docker: For example, in a script, installing Docker too if the machine does not have it
manager_desc: Both installers also take [flag_http_base_url], [flag_http_authorization] and [flag_management_secret]. They replace the server's [server_appsettings] with one that connects it to VpnHood! MANAGER, which makes it a managed server. You do not type them: the install command MANAGER shows for a server has them filled in, as Add a server shows.
uninstaller_desc: The uninstaller of a server installed without Docker takes one option, [flag_purge], which deletes the server's settings, access keys and certificates too. See Uninstall.
next_keys: Create the access keys your devices connect with, on Linux or in Docker
next_addresses: Set the IP addresses the server listens on and puts in its keys
next_domain: Use a domain name and a trusted certificate
next_blocking: Keep your server's IP address from being blocked
